solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spice: feature of Christmas morning, second to be consumed

parts.note: a card is a familiar feature of Christmas, sent to friends

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed, so the word for morning takes the word for second inside it

parts.note: MO is short for moment, a second, as in 'wait a mo'

explanation.surface: Someone describes a spice-scented Christmas morning, with a second helping about to be eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be consumed' reads as eating, but here it means one piece swallows the other: the second sits inside the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardamom is an aromatic seed pod used as a cooking spice, especially in Indian and Scandinavian baking.

clue.text: Exclusive food, but not with cold dessert

indicators.note: but not means the next piece is taken away from the word for food

parts.note: chow is slang for food
W is the abbreviation for with, as in w/
an ice is a frozen dessert

explanation.surface: Posh food, minus anything served with a chilled pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' gives W, removed from CHOW to leave CHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Choice goods are select and of the finest quality, so exclusive in the sense of high-end.

clue.text: They sell author's latest and earliest works

indicators.note: the latest letter of a word is its last one
works is read as a verb, so the letters of the next word are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer's newest and oldest books are on display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like books, but it is a verb telling you to rearrange the word earliest.
explanation.definitionFit: Retailers are shops and traders who sell goods directly to the public.

clue.text: A lot of skill to fix light

indicators.note: a lot of means most, but not all, of the word for skill: its last letter goes

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation
to clamp is to fix firmly in place

explanation.surface: It takes a fair bit of know-how to repair a lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' cuts ART to AR.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc lamp is a bright electric lamp in which the glow comes from an arc between electrodes.

clue.text: A small bird that hurts tails of all mice, right?

parts.note: ow is the cry that says something hurts

indicators.note: tails of means the last letter of each of the next words

explanation.surface: A little bird is hurting the tails of every mouse, is that right?
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young or small owl, so a small bird.

clue.text: Provide more of drink, holding favourite item back

indicators.note: holding means the word for drink has the other piece kept inside it

parts.note: to sup is to drink, especially in small mouthfuls

indicators.note: back means the word for the favourite item is read in reverse

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A host tops up the drinks while keeping a cherished possession tucked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses only the favourite, and 'holding' places it inside the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up production or supply is to increase it, so stepping up provides more of something.

clue.text: Trademark securing maybe the Queen's island in the travel industry

indicators.note: securing means the trademark letters hold the other pieces inside

parts.note: the Queen speaks of herself as 'we', so what is hers is 'our'

explanation.surface: A brand name takes in the monarch's own island to sell holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal 'we' makes the Queen's possessions 'our'; 'maybe' flags it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourism is the business of attracting and catering for visitors and holidaymakers.

clue.text: Friend suppressing greeting shows little bottle

indicators.note: suppressing means the friend's word holds the greeting down inside it

parts.note: a pal is a friend
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A pal who holds back a hello reveals a small bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass vial for medicines or perfume.

clue.text: Timely joke reflecting real life with leader being deposed

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

indicators.note: the leader being deposed means the first letter is removed

parts.note: actual means real, true to life

explanation.surface: A satirical joke about a real-life leader being overthrown lands at just the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with leader being deposed' cuts ACTUAL to CTUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Punctual means arriving on time, so timely.

clue.text: Fine coffee will take get around your motoring inconvenience

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: get around means the coffee word goes round the next piece

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A posh coffee will cheer you up while you wait for help with a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will take' is padding, apparently a slip in the clue as published; 'get around' alone does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat tyre is a punctured or deflated tyre, a common hold-up for drivers.

clue.text: Choice to keep iodine by sick American around California? It's deceptive

indicators.note: to keep means the word for choice holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: an option is a choice
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
ill means sick
US stands for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A shopper picks iodine beside an unwell American somewhere around California, then admits the whole scene is a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' splits the word for choice in two around the other pieces; 'by' and 'around' only place the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion is a visual effect that fools the eye, so it is something deceptive by nature.

clue.text: Beginnings of cool line in some computer images

indicators.note: beginnings of means the opening letter of each of the next three words is taken

parts.note: part means some, as in 'part of the cake'

explanation.surface: A designer starts a cool line using some ready-made computer pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Clip art is the stock of ready-made pictures supplied for pasting into documents, so it is a set of computer images.

clue.text: Journey permitted making a few notes

parts.note: a trip is a journey
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A traveller was allowed a journey and jotted a few notes about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' looks like jottings but is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a triplet is a group of three notes played in the time of two, so a few notes.

clue.text: Peril American writer recalled in shock — diary's contents erased

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or shock

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the writer's name runs in reverse

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

indicators.note: with its contents erased only the first and last letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: Reading an American author's recollections comes as a shock, and the diary's pages are wiped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns POE into EOP, set 'in' JAR; 'contents erased' leaves D and Y from diary's.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeopardy is danger of loss or harm, a direct synonym of peril.

clue.text: Force bar staff to accept article

parts.note: a rail is a bar

indicators.note: to accept means the staff takes the article inside

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Pressure the pub workers into taking on an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar staff' looks like pub workers but splits into bar and staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To railroad someone is to push or rush them into something, so to force.

clue.text: Coffee and brief conversation with doctor

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, a doctor

indicators.note: brief means the word for a conversation is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a chat is a conversation

explanation.surface: Coffee and a quick chat with the GP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts CHAT to CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine coffee, originally shipped from the Yemeni port of Mocha, and also a coffee-chocolate drink.

clue.text: Multiple parties? Firm came down on holding one

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: holding means the pair before it keeps the next piece inside

parts.note: alit means landed or came down
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A company descended on a party where one person is held.
explanation.walkthrough: The query flags parties as political ones; 'holding' puts the one between the two words that follow the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalition is an alliance, typically several political parties governing together.

clue.text: Clear limits to uranium, involving temperature — here's another metal

indicators.note: involving means the word for clear takes the next piece inside

parts.note: plain means clear, as in plain English

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Clear temperature limits for uranium, and here comes another metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points back to uranium, itself a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious metallic element, a second metal after uranium.

clue.text: Inclination to include finale from Berlioz, a composer

indicators.note: to include means the word for inclination takes the next piece inside it

parts.note: a list is a lean or tilt, as when a ship lists

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A musical leaning that takes in the closing passage of a Berlioz work, by way of a fellow composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' looks like a taste for something but is a ship's lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and virtuoso pianist, a contemporary of Berlioz.

clue.text: Tiny swimmer: little perch?

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
a perch and a pole are the same old unit of length

explanation.surface: A tiny swimmer, or is it a small fish?
explanation.walkthrough: 'perch' looks like the fish that suits a swimmer, but it is an old length.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a young frog or toad living in water, a small swimming creature.

clue.text: Whirling energy presented by artist in the same expressive image

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step

parts.note: idem is Latin for the same, used in references

indicators.note: whirling suggests turning round, so the word for energy is read backwards

parts.note: go means energy or drive, as in 'full of go'
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A spinning burst of energy offered by a painter in an identical, emotive picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whirling' reverses the energy, and the result with the artist goes inside the Latin word, just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideogram is a written symbol representing an idea rather than a sound, a picture that expresses meaning.

clue.text: Information on American's heart is not specific

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: Facts about an American's heart are too vague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes the middle four letters of American.
explanation.definitionFit: Generic means general, applying to a class as a whole rather than to one particular thing.

clue.text: Religious area set up in church yard? That's rather corny

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece goes inside the next pair
set up in a down clue means the word is read bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: A churchyard laid out as a holy area seems rather hackneyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses the diocese, as in a down clue, and 'in' places it between the church and yard abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesy means cheap, sentimental or trite, much the same as corny.

clue.text: Article mostly supporting meteorological report

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the article is used

parts.note: the is the definite article
under means beneath and so supporting, as in a down clue

explanation.surface: A news piece mostly backs up the weather forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' is a loud bang, not a bulletin: 'mostly' cuts THE to TH.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sound of an explosion or gunshot, and thunder is the bang that weather makes.

clue.text: Absolute flattery eschewed by Bishop

indicators.note: eschewed by means the next piece is avoided, taken out of the word

parts.note: butter is flattery, as in buttering someone up
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop shuns absolute flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter means complete or total, as in utter nonsense, so absolute.

clue.text: Seek to secure hotel in N European country

definitions.note: Finnish is the adjective for what is in or of Finland, the N European country

indicators.note: to secure means the word for seek holds the next piece fast inside it

parts.note: to fish for something is to seek it
an inn is a small hotel

explanation.surface: A traveller hunts for a hotel somewhere in northern Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Finnish describes anything belonging to Finland, the Nordic nation on the Baltic, so things found in that country.

clue.text: Old-fashioned foxtrot — out of practice, missing lead

parts.note: Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: missing lead means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: rusty means out of practice

explanation.surface: An outdated foxtrot dancer is out of practice and lacks a partner to lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foxtrot' looks like the dance but is a radio code letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusty means stale and old-fashioned in outlook, like a musty room.

clue.text: State funeral? Participation in it is no longer required

definitions.meaning: whimsically, a service held for the nation

definitions.text: Participation in it is no longer required
definitions.meaning: Compulsory peacetime military service in Britain, ended in 1960

explanation.surface: A grand state funeral, though nobody is obliged to attend any more.
explanation.walkthrough: National Service was Britain's conscription for young men, abolished in 1960; 'State funeral?' reads service as a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a ceremony for the nation and Britain's former compulsory military service, now abolished.

clue.text: Additional line encapsulating singular piece

indicators.note: encapsulating means the word for additional encloses the next piece

parts.note: more means additional, as in 'more time'
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: An extra line wraps around one lone piece of text.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small bite or fragment of food, so a little piece of something.

clue.text: Beautiful people in centre of storm encountering limits of celebrity

parts.note: the eye is the calm centre of a storm such as a hurricane
the limits of the word celebrity are C and Y, read together as C AND Y

explanation.surface: Glamorous people caught in the midst of a media storm meet the edges of fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limits of celebrity' gives C and Y, and the phrase 'C and Y' is spelt out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye candy is slang for people attractive to look at but offering little else.
